{{Short description|Theorem in measure theory}}
{{More citations needed|date=March 2011}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Fatou–Lebesgue theorem''' establishes a chain of [[inequality (mathematics)|inequalities]] relating the [[integral]]s (in the sense of [[Lebesgue integration|Lebesgue]]) of the [[limit superior and limit inferior|limit inferior]] and the [[limit superior and limit inferior|limit superior]] of a [[sequence]] of [[function (mathematics)|function]]s to the limit inferior and the limit superior of integrals of these functions.  The theorem is named after [[Pierre Fatou]] and [[Henri Léon Lebesgue]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Mackevicius |first=Vigirdas |title=Integral and Measure: From Rather Simple to Rather Complex |date=September 2014 |publisher=Wiley-ISTE |isbn=978-1-119-03749-1 |edition=1st |pages=119–132 |language=en}}</ref>

If the sequence of functions converges [[pointwise convergence|pointwise]], the inequalities turn into [[equality (mathematics)|equalities]] and the theorem reduces to Lebesgue's [[dominated convergence theorem]].

==Statement of the theorem==
Let ''f''<sub>1</sub>, ''f''<sub>2</sub>, ... denote a sequence of [[real number|real]]-valued [[measurable function|measurable]] functions defined on a [[measure space]] (''S'',''Σ'',''μ''). If there exists a Lebesgue-integrable function ''g'' on ''S'' which dominates the sequence in absolute value, meaning that |''f''<sub>''n''</sub>|&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''g'' for all [[natural number]]s ''n'', then all ''f''<sub>''n''</sub> as well as the limit inferior and the limit superior of the ''f''<sub>''n''</sub> are integrable and
:<math>
\int_S \liminf_{n\to\infty} f_n\,d\mu
\le \liminf_{n\to\infty} \int_S f_n\,d\mu
\le \limsup_{n\to\infty} \int_S f_n\,d\mu
\le \int_S \limsup_{n\to\infty} f_n\,d\mu\,.
</math>
Here the limit inferior and the limit superior of the ''f''<sub>''n''</sub> are taken pointwise. The integral of the absolute value of these limiting functions is bounded above by the integral of ''g''.

Since the middle inequality (for sequences of real numbers) is always true, the directions of the other inequalities are easy to remember.

==Proof==
All ''f''<sub>''n''</sub> as well as the limit inferior and the limit superior of the ''f''<sub>''n''</sub> are measurable and dominated in absolute value by ''g'', hence integrable.

Using
[[Lebesgue_integral#Basic_theorems_of_the_Lebesgue_integral|linearity of the Lebesgue integral]] and applying [[Fatou's lemma]] to the non-negative functions <math>f_n + g</math> we get
<math display ="block> \int_X \liminf_{n \to\infty} f_n \,d\mu + \int_X g \,d\mu = \int_X \liminf_{n \to \infty} (f_n + g) \le \liminf_{n \to \infty} \int_X (f_n + g) \, d\mu =\liminf_{n \to \infty} \int_X f_n \,d\mu + \int_X g \, d\mu.</math>
Cancelling the finite(!) <math>\int_X g \,d\mu</math> term we get the first inequality. The second inequality is the elementary inequality between <math>\liminf</math> and <math>\limsup</math>. 
The last inequality follows by applying [[Fatou's_lemma#Reverse_Fatou_lemma|reverse Fatou lemma]], i.e. applying the Fatou lemma to the non-negative functions <math>g-f_n</math>, and again (up to sign) cancelling the finite <math>\int_X g \,d\mu</math> term.

Finally, since <math>\limsup_n |f_n| \le g</math>,

:<math>\max\left(\left|\int_S \liminf_{n\to\infty} f_n\,d\mu\right|
,  \left|\int_S \limsup_{n\to\infty} f_n\,d\mu\right|
\right) \le\int_S \max\left(\left|\liminf_{n\to\infty} f_n\right|, \left|\limsup_{n\to \infty} f_n\right|\right)\, d\mu
\le\int_S \limsup_{n\to\infty} |f_n|\,d\mu
\le\int_S g\,d\mu</math>

by the [[Lebesgue_integral#Basic_theorems_of_the_Lebesgue_integral|monotonicity of the Lebesgue integral]].
